title: Equal latitude-band weights left a positive Indian-minus-Atlantic steric lag contrast in NOAA upper-ocean fields for 2005-2025
abstract: We tested whether latitude coverage can account for a reported basin difference in steric sea-level time scales. We used NOAA NCEI upper-700-m seasonal fields for 2005-2025 and gave both basins equal weights in nine latitude bands from 60 S to 30 N. The score compares total-to-thermal mean squared-change ratios at one-season and one-year lags. The Indian-minus-Atlantic log lag contrast was 0.0723, with conditional 95% three-year block limits of 0.0242 to 0.1160. The sign held with other block lengths and without trend removal. The Indian lag contrast alone was uncertain. Equal latitude-band weights did not remove the basin difference. Secondary zone tests placed the clearest contrast between 30 S and the equator. One mapped product, 19 start years, selected latitude bands, and uncertainty conditional on fitted residuals limit inference. This is not an independent salinity or causal test. The package gives code, aggregate evidence, bootstrap draws, source hashes, audits, and a retrieval recipe. Raw fields stay external.

display.caption: Equal latitude-band scores and paired uncertainty. The Indian-minus-Atlantic lag contrast remains positive with common band weights. Secondary zone intervals are unadjusted.
